title: A gold standard for literary adaptation
gist: Daniel Rey reviews Zoe Kazan's seven-part Netflix adaptation of East of Eden, praising its fuller, more human Cathy (Florence Pugh) and mostly superb script while noting stilted monologues and a slow start. He calls it a gold standard for literary adaptation.

insights.claim: Zoe Kazan's seven-part Netflix East of Eden improves on her grandfather Elia Kazan's 1955 film by restoring Lee and developing Cathy, filling gaps left by Steinbeck.
insights.speaker: Daniel Rey
insights.so_what: Positive critical reception supports Netflix's prestige literary-adaptation slate.

insights.claim: The series makes Cathy the key player by opening with her, and Florence Pugh plays her greyer and more human than Steinbeck's near-satanic villain.
insights.speaker: Daniel Rey
insights.so_what: Casting and script choices central to the show's praise.
insights.quote: Zoe Kazan’s Cathy (Florence Pugh) is greyer.

insights.claim: Kazan's long Steinbeck monologues, repeated almost verbatim, and the occasional voice-of-God narration sound out of kilter with her simpler script.
insights.speaker: Daniel Rey
insights.so_what: Critique suggests faithful dialogue transfer does not always work on screen.
insights.locator: Kazan often incorporates Steinbeck’s original dialogue

insights.claim: The staccato first half-hour, with Adam and Charles each played by three actors, makes it hard to invest before the show becomes compelling.
insights.speaker: Daniel Rey
insights.so_what: Early pacing is a possible drop-off point for viewers.
insights.locator: However, once we get past that staccato start
